description: FIND-003 ('self-fix.sh fired-and-forgot; no programmatic verification of the fix') is NOT resolved, only reworded. self-fix.sh now writes a RESULT marker file (line 30, 'RUNNING <ts>') and its prose TASK (lines 31-38) instructs the spawned Opus session to eventually write 'SUCCESS <ts> <evidence>' or 'FAIL <ts> <why>' to that same file (step 5). But self-fix.sh itself never reads back or validates that RESULT file's final content -- it spawns the tmux session at line 39 and returns immediately. Nothing in the codebase re-curls the 'evidence' URL the fixer claims, re-runs the originally-failing check, or verifies the fixer actually committed anything. The only consumer of the RESULT file is verify-loops.sh:33 (`cat "$r"`), which is a MANUAL diagnostic script (see FIND-016) that merely prints whatever the fixer wrote -- it does not independently verify the claim. This means a fixer that writes 'SUCCESS ... published https://fake-or-stale-url' is indistinguishable from a real fix: the same LLM that performed the fix is also the sole grader of its own success, with zero independent/automated check. This directly contradicts the system's own anti-fake mandate ('Success = only REAL observable side-effects... never faked/masked').
